request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is

batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle is now all-or-nothing, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves now**
- If any selected claim would be refused, nothing is settled. That covers anything a single settle refuses, plus an id that isn't on the sheet. Every claim counts as refused, nothing is stored, no audit line is written and no batch number is used up. A claim that goes to PENDING still counts as settled.
- If none would be refused, the claims settle in list order as before. After their own lines, one more line is written: `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=… by=… batch=<n> count=<claims in the batch> total=<frozen figures of the SETTLED ones added up>`. PENDING claims count towards `count` but not `total`.

**Changes**
- **`claim/SettleClaims.java`**: runs the whole batch so it can be undone. On the first refusal it stops, undoes the store changes and drops the audit lines. Otherwise it keeps everything and adds the `BATCH_SETTLED` line.
- **`claim/ClaimRepository.java`**: new `keepOnly(...)`, which runs work in a Spring `TransactionTemplate` and rolls it back if the work reports failure. It uses a savepoint if a transaction is already open.
- **`Audit.java`**: new `hold()` and `release(write)`. Audit lines made during the batch are held back, then written in order or thrown away.
- I updated the comments in `bulk-settle.POST.yml` and `bulk.slot.tsx` to say it's all-or-nothing.

**Something you may want to look into:** my first attempt rolled back to a savepoint on the request's connection, and it didn't work. A debug line showed that inside this endpoint's settle step, no Spring transaction is active and the connection is in auto-commit mode. So each statement commits on its own, even though the step is marked `govern: [ transaction ]`. That's why I bound the transaction myself in `keepOnly`. It probably means other "transactional" endpoints aren't atomic either. I didn't investigate further because it's outside this change.

probe.probe_text:
# Figures and rules on the sheet, as the code stands now

I changed nothing. All money is held to two decimals.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### A. Which claims count

- **Status.** `ClaimStatus` moves DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED, with PENDING in between when a settle needs approval. `counts()` is true for OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. `isOpen()` is true for OPEN and PENDING: only these "live" claims go overdue, gain a late charge and can be held.
- **`Rollup.counts`** decides whether a claim is in the live totals. It must have a counting status, must not be `held`, and must not be `isDeferredOn(today)`.
- **`Rollup.held`** leaves a claim out when all of these are true:
  - it is OPEN or PENDING;
  - it is not `isBound()`;
  - either its date falls in one of its person's holds (`Person.heldOn` / `HoldSpan.covers`, both ends inclusive, a blank end is open) or the person has reached retirement (`Person.retiredOn(today)`, meaning today is on or after `retiredFrom`).
- **`Claim.isDeferredOn(today)`**: an OPEN claim whose `deferredUntil` is after today. It counts in no total, is not overdue, gets no late charge, cannot be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound.
- **Bound.** `isStated()` means the last statement bound the claim. `isBound()` means stated and not PENDING. A PENDING claim shows its live figure, and goes back to its bound figure if it is rejected back to OPEN.
- **VOID.** A voided SETTLED claim keeps its frozen `settledDue`, which still shows, but it counts in no total.

### B. A claim's figures

- **`claim-amount`** and **`claim-date`**.
  - **Amount (`ClaimAmount`):** up to 12 digits and 2 decimals, 0.00 or more.
  - **Corrections:** a negative amount is a correction (`isCorrection`). `RefuseBadCorrection` requires it to name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person, and refuses a non-negative claim that names one.
- **Date.**
  - A blank date on add, paste or quick-add takes `entryDate` (the `entry-date` setting if set, else the sheet's today).
  - A blank date on edit takes the sheet's today instead (`ApplyClaim`).
- **The claim's figure** (`Rollup.figure`, `ApplyClaimStatus.dueNow`, front end `claimFigureCents`), in this order:
  1. its `settledDue`;
  2. else its `statedDue`, if `isBound()` (null shows as n/a);
  3. else `figureAt(rate, rounding)`: amount × rate ÷ 100, set to 2 decimals.
     - The rate is `rateOn` / `RateRepository.find`: the rate of the grade the person had on the claim's date (`Person.gradeOn(date)`), picking the one with the latest from-date on or before that date. A blank from-date counts as the earliest. There is no rate if the date is after that rate's to-date.
- **Rounding (`LateCharge.rounding`).**
  - HALF_UP when the claim's `roundOn` is before the `policy-date`; HALF_EVEN on or after it.
  - A blank policy date means the sheet's today.
  - `roundOn` is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects (the `corrected_date` subquery; front end `dateOfNumber`).
- **`claim-due`** is `LateCharge.due` (front end `claimDueCents`):
  - a settled claim shows its `settledDue` exactly as stored;
  - otherwise it is the greater of `floor(claim date)` and figure + `on()` (the late charge);
  - a correction has no floor and no late charge;
  - with no figure it shows n/a.
- **Late charge (`LateCharge.onAsOpen`).**
  - `lateFrom` = `dueBy` + `grace(grade on claim date, claim date)`.
  - For each full 30 days since `lateFrom`, it adds `latePct(lateFrom + 30n)` × (figure + charge so far), each step rounded as the claim rounds. The charge compounds.
  - It is never bound by a statement. Settling freezes it into the settled due.
- **`claim-due-by`.**
  - It is `HolidayRepository.businessDay(date, terms, holidays)`: the `terms`-th weekday after the date that is not a holiday.
  - `terms` is fixed when the claim is added, by `DatedSettings.terms(person, date)`: the person's own terms, else the grade's `terms-<g>`, else the sheet's `terms` (14 by default).
  - `dueBy` is stored at insert. `due_from` keeps the date the claim was added with, so neither an edit nor a re-date moves it.
  - Adding a holiday runs `ClaimRepository.refix`. That re-fixes every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and whose due-by is on or after the new holiday.
- **`claim-overdue`** (`LateCharge.overdue`, front end `useIsOverdue`): OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom` is before today.
- **`claim-number`.**
  - It is given at open, and only after the status change has succeeded, so a refused open uses up no number.
  - By default it is `nextNumber(sheet)`.
  - While `period-numbering-from` is set and today is on or after it, the number is `<period name>-<n>` within the period containing the claim's due-by, or `X-<n>` when no period contains it.
  - A voided claim keeps its number.
- **Other per-claim flags and values:**
  - `claim-period` is the period that contains the claim's **due-by**, not its date.
  - `claim-late-entry` is set when the claim's due-by was in a soft-closed period when it was added (`markLate`).
  - `claim-stated` is yes or no.
  - The rest are shown as stored: `claim-deferred` / `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-reminded` (once per sheet-today), `claim-opened-by`, `claim-batch`, `claim-void-reason`, `claim-tags` (lower-cased, sorted, duplicates removed), `claim-ref` (unique on the sheet, case ignored).

### C. A person's figures

- **`person-claimed`**: the amounts of the person's counting claims (`sumAmounts`).
- **`person-due-total`** (`Rollup.snapshot`, front end `useDueParts` + `useDueTotals`):
  - the sum of the person's counting claims' dues;
  - shown as n/a when the grade they hold today has no rate today and no claim is "kept". A claim is kept when it has a settled or bound figure, or has a figure and is at another grade or dated on or before today;
  - otherwise held to `SettingRepository.capped`, the `cap` in force on today. An n/a total is not capped.
- **Other person figures:**
  - **Excess:** `person-excess` is the uncapped total minus the cap.
  - **Settled and open:** `person-settled-total` and `person-open-total` split the uncapped total by SETTLED versus OPEN/PENDING.
  - **Overdue:** `person-overdue-count` and `person-overdue-total` cover counting overdue claims, uncapped.
  - **Ageing:** `person-aged-0-30`, `person-aged-31-60` and `person-aged-61` split the due of counting OPEN and PENDING claims by days from the claim's date to today.
  - **Active:** `person-active` is yes when they have a counting OPEN or PENDING claim dated in the 30 days up to today.
  - **Backing:** `person-backing` is the patrons' SETTLED `settledDue` on claims dated in the last 90 days.
  - **Periods:** `person-period-<name>-due-total`: see section E.
  - **Statements:** `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total` and `person-statement-date`.
  - **Grade:** `person-grade` is the grade in force on the sheet's today (`gradeOn`, latest from-date wins).
  - **Retirement and terms:** `person-retired-from` and `person-terms`.

### D. Sheet totals

- **`rollup-claimed-total`** adds up everyone's claimed. It is not trimmed.
- **`rollup-due-total`** and **`header-due-total`** add up the people's due-totals, skipping n/a, and are `trimmed`: with 3 or more people, the single highest and the single lowest are left out.
- **`rollup-overdue-total`** and **`header-overdue-total`** are trimmed the same way. **`rollup-overdue-count`** is not.
- **`rollup-settled-total`** and **`rollup-open-total`** are not trimmed.
- **`tag-<t>-due-total`** and **`month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total`** add up the dues of counting claims. A claim with two tags counts under both.
- **`summary-grade-<g>-*`**:
  - the count covers people on that grade today, leaving out anyone with a `retiredFrom` at all;
  - the due-total adds up those people's capped totals;
  - active is the number of those people who are active.
- **`summary-status-*-count`**, **`header-claims-*-count`** and **`summary-void-<reason>-count`** are plain counts.
- **Audit:** after every change, `Rollup.record` writes a `ROLLUP` line for each person whose figures moved, then a `TOTALS` line if any of the three sheet totals moved.

### E. Periods and what gets frozen

- **Belonging.** A claim belongs to the period that contains its **due-by**.
- **Live period total.** `dueBetweenByPerson` and front end `usePeriodDueTotal` add up each claim's figure as it stands now. A claim counts by the status its log records at the end of the period's to-date (`statusesAsOf`), but holds and deferral are applied by its status now (`countsAs`).
- **Close** (`ClosePeriod`) and **soft-close** (`SoftClosePeriod`) both freeze `closedTotal` and `personTotals`.
  - On screen, `period-due-total` and `person-period-*` then show the frozen figures. A person added after the freeze shows 0.00.
  - A **closed** period refuses every change to its claims (`RefuseClosedClaim` / `RefuseClosedNewDate`). The check is on the claim's due-by, including the due-by a new claim would get.
  - A **soft-closed** period still allows changes; new claims in it are marked as late entries.
- **Who may act.** Close and soft-close need the `perm-close` permission (clerk and steward while blank). Reopen needs `perm-reopen` (steward while blank). Reopening clears the frozen figures.
- **Auto-close.** `AutoClosePeriods` runs when the sheet's today is set. With `grace-days` set, it closes every open period whose to-date + grace days is before the new today, and writes `auto=yes`.
- **Generate.** `GeneratePeriods` makes one `yyyy-mm` period per month, skipping names already used and any overlaps.
- **Add.** `CheckPeriod` refuses a duplicate name, an overlap, or a to-date before the from-date.

### F. What else freezes or changes figures

- **Settle** (`ApplyClaimStatus`) freezes `settledDue`: the live due with the late charge as of today and the floor, or the bound figure plus charge and floor. It stays null, and the due stays live, when there is no rate.
- **Statement** (`TakeStatement`):
  - binds every counting claim to its *figure*, with no late charge and no floor, and unbinds the rest;
  - records the person's due-total, capped, or n/a;
  - can be taken as of a past date, using `SheetHistory` snapshots. A date after today is refused, and so is one before the person was on the sheet.
  - **Cancel** (`CancelStatement`) is steward-only. It unbinds every claim the person has; earlier bindings are not restored.
- **Re-settle** (`ApplyResettle`, steward-only): re-freezes a settled claim at `dueAsOpen`.
- **Split** (`ApplySplit`):
  - the original claim keeps the rest of the amount and loses its binding;
  - the new claim is OPEN, gets the next number and its own terms, and records `splitFrom`.
- **Reassign** (`ApplyReassign`):
  - needs `perm-reassign` (steward while blank), and works on DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claims only;
  - the claim keeps its number, loses its binding, and is relisted as the new person's newest claim;
  - it is refused if the target person retired before the claim's date.
- **Re-date** (`ApplyRedate`, steward-only, OPEN or PENDING only): the due-by, any binding, the period and the number all stay.
- **Hold** (`HoldPerson`): a blank from-date means today; a blank to-date means open-ended. **Retire** (`RetirePerson`): a blank date means today, and it can happen only once.
- **Dated settings.** The value in force on a date is the latest one from on or before it (`DatedSettings.on`). These are dated:
  - `floor` (default 1.00), `terms` (default 14), `terms-<g>`, `grace-<g>`;
  - `late-pct` (default 0.00);
  - `cap`, `clerk-limit`, `proof-threshold`, `proof-threshold-<g>`, `note-threshold`.

  These are undated: `policy-date`, `period-numbering-from`, `entry-date`, `grace-days`, and the `perm-*` permissions.

### G. Who may do what (`ApplyClaimStatus` and others)

- **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`):
  - a user with no assigned role is a clerk;
  - a `viewer` may change nothing (`RefuseViewer`, which also refuses any change to an archived sheet);
  - a delegation (`actingFor`) makes a user a steward while the sheet's today is inside its range and the delegating user is still a steward.
- **Status moves** follow `canBecome`. Open, settle and void also need `perm-open` / `perm-settle` / `perm-void` (clerk and steward while blank).
- **Who cannot settle or approve:** the `openedBy` user and the `editedBy` user.
- **Settling above the limit:** a clerk's settle whose due is above `clerk-limit(today)` becomes PENDING. Only a steward approves (it settles at the live due) or rejects (back to OPEN, a reason required).
- **Proof:** a settle or approve with 0 proofs whose due is above `proofThreshold(grade on date, date)` is refused. An n/a due is within any limit.
- **Note:** opening a claim with an empty note is refused when its `dueAsOpen` is above `note-threshold(claim date)`.
- **Voiding:**
  - a SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward, and only within `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS` (7) of the last SETTLED log date;
  - while the sheet has void reasons, a void must give one from the list.
- **Editing:** only a DRAFT can be edited (`RefuseNonDraftEdit`). An edit is refused while another user holds the claim lock. A date after retirement is refused.
- **Other actions:**
  - proofs cannot be added to SETTLED or VOID claims;
  - defer only for an OPEN claim, to a date after today;
  - remind only an OPEN or PENDING claim, once per day.
- **Bulk actions:**
  - **Bulk settle** is all-or-nothing. It also writes `BATCH_SETTLED` and a batch number.
  - **Bulk open and bulk reassign** go claim by claim; any claim that is refused is counted as refused.
  - **Paste** (`AddPastedClaims`) checks every line first, and one refused line refuses the whole paste. The claims are added as DRAFT.
  - **Quick-add** (`ResolvePerson`) creates a grade-A person if the name is new.
- **Archive** is steward-only. While the screen shows the sheet as of a date, every change is refused (`RefuseAsOfChanges`).

### Inconsistencies I noticed

These are worth knowing before changing anything:

1. **Held stated PENDING claims.** The back end's live `held` checks `isBound()`. Its period totals (`countsAs`) and the front end's `counts` check `stated`. So a stated PENDING claim inside a hold is left out of the audit `ROLLUP` but included in the totals on screen.
2. **Holiday re-fix.** `refix` works due-by out again from `claim.getDate()`, not from `dueFrom`. A re-dated claim's due-by can therefore move after all, which contradicts `ApplyRedate`'s promise that its due-by stays.
3. **Blank date on edit.** An edit with a blank date takes the sheet's today, while add, paste and quick-add take the entry date. `ValidatePaste`'s comment also says "today".
4. **Unrestricted settings.** Rates, settings, holidays and role assignment are refused only for viewers. Any clerk can change permissions or make themselves a steward.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard. The rules aren't in one place: they are spread over roughly 340 small Java step classes, wired together in 59 YAML pipelines. The front end independently re-implements the same due, late-charge, floor, cap, hold and trimming logic in `useRates.ts`, `useClaims.ts`, `rates.slot.tsx`, `overdue.slot.tsx`, `periods.slot.tsx` and others, so the screen's figures are computed separately from the server's. Even on the server, the same rules are copied between `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `ApplyClaimStatus` and `ApplyResettle`, and those copies have already drifted apart (see the inconsistencies above). The long Javadoc on each class is the most reliable map, but a new developer would need to read both halves of the app side by side to know what any one figure really is.
